written_by_evidence: components/video-production/machine/work_queue.py files ONE record per claim / progress / release, committed straight onto origin/main (commit-tree + push, never through a working tree) — 2026-10-10, so a second video editor's computer and the owner's Mac work the song-ad / video line without both taking the same ad
title: Video work queue — which computer is working which ad
note: One append-only record per act on one ad (a brief id): `claim` (this machine takes the ad), `progress` (the ad reached a stage; also keeps the claim fresh) and `release` (the machine lets it go). Current state is FOLDED, never stored: the latest claim not followed by the same machine's release (or a forced release) is the owner, and the owner's latest claim/progress is its last progress. A claim whose owner filed nothing for the stale window (6 hours by default) may be taken over; the new claim carries `takeover_of`. A claim counts only once it is on origin/main — offline means not claimed. Stages, in order: song, b-roll, cut, hooks, card, done (a format with no song skips the song stage). The stage a machine reports is what ITS runs show; the status page takes the furthest of that and what the reading machine's own runs and the Drive card folders show. Records are written by work_queue.py, never by hand.

verdict_fields.note: the computer that filed it — VIDEO_QUEUE_MACHINE, else the host name, as a slug. Ownership is per MACHINE: the same person on two computers is two claimants.
who was at it — VIDEO_QUEUE_PERSON, else the part of git user.email before the @; also the record's `reviewer`
the act's UTC time to the microsecond; orders two acts filed in one second. `created` stays the plane's to-the-second stamp.
on claim and progress: the stage the filing machine's own runs showed
the brand folder of the run the filing machine has for this ad, when it has one
the run label (runs/video-production/<brand>/<label>/), when the filing machine has one
on a claim that replaced a stale one: {machine, person, last_at} of the claim it replaced
on a release filed by a machine that is not the owner (work_queue.py release --force)
